offerings.title: Ways to spend time here
offerings.intro: Come for a class, book the sauna, hire the Oasis Studio for your own work, or stay the night in the valley.

schedule.title: What runs at Amara Moon
schedule.intro: Classes are small by design. Arrive a few minutes early, and bring nothing but yourself — mats and props are here.
schedule.note: Days and times for the coming season are being finalised. Everything below runs here — tell us what you would like to join and we will let you know when it is on.
schedule.bookingBody: Sauna sessions can be booked and paid for online. For classes and studio hire, send us a note and we will confirm your place.

gallery.title: A look around
gallery.intro: Ten minutes from Hout Bay village, at the foot of the Orangekloof valley.
gallery.closingLine: Come and see it for yourself.

workWithUs.title: Share your practice in the valley
workWithUs.intro: We are inviting experienced teachers to join our growing community. Amara Moon is small and family run, and the people who teach here shape what it becomes.
workWithUs.introduceBody: Tell us what you do and what you have in mind, a link to your website or Instagram helps us see your work. We read these ourselves and reply properly.

lookingFor.title: Teachers
lookingFor.body: Experienced yoga, movement, breathwork and meditation teachers who want a regular slot in the shala or a one-off workshop.

lookingFor.title: Retreat hosts
lookingFor.body: Facilitators looking for a venue with accommodation, a pool and sauna, and private access to the mountain.

lookingFor.title: Practitioners
lookingFor.body: Massage therapists, bodyworkers and sound practitioners who would like to see clients here.

lookingFor.title: Creatives
lookingFor.body: Photographers, writers and makers whose work sits alongside what we do in the valley.

contact.title: Say hello
contact.intro: Questions about a class, hiring the studio, or staying the night? Send us a note and we'll come back to you.
contact.gettingHere: Ten minutes from Hout Bay village, at the foot of the Orangekloof valley. There is parking on site, and private access to the mountain trails.
